propwash.video.config.title: Video
propwash.video.config.fov.tooltip: Custom horizontal field of view of the creative goggles. Wide values feel faster but distort more.
propwash.video.config.fov_source.tooltip: Creative goggles: field of view like the camera in the drone's video unit, or set freely (sandbox).
propwash.video.config.format.tooltip: 16:9 fills the whole window as before. 4:3 shows the image like a 4:3 camera in 4:3 goggles: the same field of view across, more image above and below, black bars left and right; the OSD sits inside the 4:3 image. Auto follows the drone's video system: analog 4:3, digital 16:9 – also while spectating. Action cam recordings stay 16:9.
propwash.video.config.format_line.boxed: Image format 4:3: %s° wide × %s° high – more image above and below, black bars left and right.
propwash.video.config.format_line.wide: Image format 16:9: %s° wide × %s° high, fills the whole window.
propwash.video.config.format_line.fishey: Image format 4:3 with fisheye: %s° wide × %s° high, %s° diagonal – black bars left and right.
Image format 16:9 with fisheye: %s° wide × %s° high, %s° diagonal, fills the whole window.
propwash.video.config.lens.tooltip: How strongly the FPV image bends like a real fisheye lens. The width of the field of view always stays that of the video module. 0 %% is flat like Minecraft: straight lines stay straight, the centre is perfectly sharp but looks smaller and farther away. %s %% (default) is a real FPV camera: centre bigger and closer, edges squeezed and bent – speed feels like in a real FPV feed. Up to 100 %% the edges are squeezed even more and the centre gets bigger and a little softer, because Propwash renders a wider image and de-warps it.
propwash.video.config.fov_module.tooltip: The field of view comes from the camera in the drone's video unit – just like in real life. Analog and digital goggles use it; a different field of view means a different video unit.
propwash.video.config.fov_line.module: Camera of the video unit “%s”: %s° horizontal.
propwash.video.config.fov_line.fallback: Video unit “%s” without its own value: %s° horizontal (default of the video system).
propwash.video.config.fov_line.none: The field of view comes from the camera in the video unit of the drone you fly or hold.
propwash.video.config.fov_line.own: Creative goggles with a custom field of view: %s° horizontal, independent of the video unit.
propwash.video.config.strength.tooltip: How strongly image interference is shown. Signal loss and frozen frames still happen at 0%%.
propwash.video.config.camera_shake.toolt: Fine shake of the FPV image like a real camera on the frame: a faint motor buzz (clearly stronger with damaged props or motors), plus buffeting in your own prop wash, close to the ground and walls at low speed, and a jolt on hard punch-outs. At high speed the image stays calm. Image only, flight physics stay unchanged. 100%% is the default, 0%% turns it off.
propwash.video.config.reduce_flicker.too: Softens fast brightness changes, rolling bars and picture rolls, fades signal loss in gently and lowers the noise rate. Recommended for light sensitivity.
propwash.video.config.renderer.tooltip: “Full” shows every image effect. The simple overlay is lighter and works with shader packs; it is used automatically when the full effects can't run.
propwash.video.config.led_lighting.toolt: Just for you: at night and in caves the LED strip lights up the FPV view in a light cone. Turn it off if the view goes black or glitchy with it on your computer. The LEDs themselves and what other players see stay the same.
propwash.video.config.retry.tooltip: Try the video or headlight shader again after an error (for example after switching resource packs or graphics drivers).
propwash.video.config.creative.latency.t: Delay between the drone camera and the goggles. Switching to "own" starts the slider at the video transmitter's latency; below it, laps count as assisted.
propwash.video.config.latency_source.too: Creative goggles: picture delayed like the drone's video transmitter (laps count) or set freely. Less latency than the transmitter doesn't count for leaderboards; the creative goggles' range, obstacles and breakup never count as a flight aid.
propwash.video.config.creative.range.too: Distance at which the video and radio signal start to fade. With a limited range the picture behaves like the drone's video system; unlimited lifts the radio range too.
propwash.video.config.creative.noise.too: Extra analog noise, independent of the signal.
propwash.video.config.creative.obstructi: Blocks between you and the drone weaken the signal. Only applies with a limited range.
propwash.video.config.no_goggles: Put on FPV goggles – this tab then shows the settings of exactly those goggles. Which goggles you wear decides what applies; it cannot be switched here.

propwash.video.record.hud.tip.graphics: Tip: lower shaders/graphics or set an FPS limit

propwash.video.record.hud.tip.busy: Tip: close programs that keep the processor or graphics card busy
propwash.video.record.hud.tip.disk: Tip: record to an SSD or close programs that keep the drive busy
propwash.video.record.hud.tip.space: Tip: free up disk space for the frame buffer
propwash.video.record.tab.title: Action cam
propwash.video.record.tab.resolution.too: Video size (16:9). The Light cam goes up to 1080p, the Heavy cam up to 1440p. Larger means sharper, but more processing and bigger files.
propwash.video.record.tab.fps.tooltip: Frames per second in the video. If the game runs slower, the video repeats frames so length and speed stay right.
propwash.video.record.tab.quality.toolti: High: close to lossless, even in dark scenes and fast pans. At %s about %s MB per minute, at most %s MB/min.
Standard: clean picture with manageable files, recommended. At %s about %s MB per minute, at most %s MB/min. Quality stays the same, calm scenes simply get smaller.
Small: small files for sharing, fine detail gets softer. At %s about %s MB per minute, at most %s MB/min.
Raw camera image, like the Light cam, which has no stabilization.
Heavy cam only: smooths fast shakes using the known camera attitude; the picture gets tighter by the crop shown under Strength.
propwash.video.record.tab.encoder.toolti: Uses a hardware encoder of your graphics card or processor (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMD AMF, VideoToolbox) if ffmpeg is installed – that frees the processor and handles 1080p60 easily. Without ffmpeg, or if the hardware encoder fails, Propwash's own encoder takes over. Whether ffmpeg was found is shown under “Faster recording with ffmpeg” below.
Always records with Propwash's own encoder on the processor – no extra program needed. It uses several processor cores; on slower computers choose 720p or 30 fps.
propwash.video.record.tab.strength.toolt: How strongly the Heavy cam steadies its picture. More strength holds the picture calmer and the horizon over a wider bank angle, but crops tighter. The picture is cut from the full-resolution game image before it is scaled down: if your game window is larger than the video by at least the crop factor, stabilizing costs no sharpness.
propwash.video.record.tab.status.encoder: Encoder: %s via ffmpeg (hardware) – the processor stays free for the game.
Encoder: Propwash (CPU, %s threads) – no ffmpeg found.
Encoder: Propwash (CPU, %s threads) – no usable hardware encoder.
Hardware encoder failed (%s) – Propwash's encoder (CPU) until you press “Test” or restart the game.
propwash.video.record.tab.ffmpeg.path.to: Leave empty: Propwash finds ffmpeg by itself – on the PATH, where Homebrew, MacPorts, WinGet, Scoop, Chocolatey and Linux packages install it, and in the folder propwash/ffmpeg in the game directory. Only if yours is somewhere else: enter the path of the ffmpeg program or its folder (or drop the file onto this window) and press “Test”.
propwash.video.record.tab.ffmpeg.test.to: Looks for ffmpeg again and encodes a short test clip with every hardware encoder of this computer. Press it after installing ffmpeg while the game is running.
propwash.video.record.tab.ffmpeg.guide.t:
Opens the guide “Faster recording with ffmpeg” in your browser: installing it on Windows, macOS and Linux and how to check that it works.
%s

ffmpeg at %s does not start (%s) – Propwash's own encoder records on the processor.

%s found (%s), but no hardware encoder works (%s) – Propwash's own encoder records on the processor.

There is no program at the entered path.

propwash.video.record.hud.encoder.no_ffm: Encoder: Propwash (CPU) – faster with ffmpeg, see the “Action cam” tab
propwash.video.record.hud.encoder.checki: Encoder: Propwash (CPU) – the ffmpeg check was still running
propwash.video.record.hud.encoder.no_har: Encoder: Propwash (CPU) – no usable hardware encoder, see the “Action cam” tab
propwash.video.record.tab.status.crop.lo: Stabilization crop ×%s: no loss of sharpness with this window (%s×%s).
propwash.video.record.tab.status.crop.up: Stabilization crop ×%s: the picture is scaled up by %s%% with this window (%s×%s) – a larger game window keeps it sharp.
Heavy cam only: smooths and keeps the horizon level – at 50% strength up to about ±22° of bank, beyond that it follows; the picture gets much tighter.
propwash.video.record.tab.audio.tooltip: Records your drone's motor sound too, like the microphone of a real action cam on the frame (AAC in MP4, plays everywhere). Other game sounds are not included.
propwash.video.record.tab.auto.tooltip: Starts recording automatically when you arm in FPV and stops it when you disarm.
propwash.video.record.tab.indicator.tool: Shows notices at the top center while recording (paused, cam battery low, and which part of the computer limits the recording – game, graphics card, encoder, drive or frame buffer – with a tip) and the saving progress outside FPV. The REC indicator itself is an OSD element: show, hide or move it in the “OSD” tab. Neither ever appears in the video.
propwash.video.record.tab.grain.tooltip: Subtle sensor noise only in very dark parts of the picture, like a real small camera (a little more on the Light cam than on the Heavy cam). Off = noise-free picture.
propwash.video.record.tab.recordings.too: All videos with thumbnail, date, length and size – play, delete or open the folder. It also shows how far saving has got.
propwash.video.record.tab.open_folder.to: Opens the propwash/recordings folder in the game directory.
propwash.video.record.tab.hint: %1$s starts and stops recording while flying FPV (rebind it in the “Keys” tab). On the radio: function “%2$s” in the “Modes” tab – a switch records while it is on, a button starts and stops with every press. The REC indicator is an OSD element in the “OSD” tab. The action cam records the clean camera image without OSD and without radio interference, as MP4 (H.264, optionally with sound).
propwash.video.record.tab.status.no_dron: No drone in hand or in flight.
propwash.video.record.tab.status.flight_: Powered by the flight battery: %s W, no separate runtime limit.
propwash.video.recordings.title: Recordings
propwash.video.recordings.empty.hint: Mount an action cam on top of your drone in the workbench and press %s while flying FPV – or put the “Record” function on a switch of your radio.
propwash.video.channel.choice.tip:
Automatic: when the drone takes off, the server gives it a channel no other pilot is using.
Fixed channel: always stays the same, like a VTX you set by hand.
propwash.video.channel.label: %s · %s MHz
propwash.video.channel.no_drone: No drone: hold a drone or fly one to set its channel.
propwash.video.channel.info_auto: Automatic: at takeoff the server picks a free channel – R1, R2, F2, F4, R7 and R8 first, the proven race line-up. The channel is shown in the OSD (VTX).
propwash.video.channel.info_manual: Fixed channel: the server never changes it – agree on channels with the other pilots. The channel is shown in the OSD (VTX).
propwash.video.spectate.goggles: Your goggles receive %s. Pick a channel to spectate – the picture depends on how far you are from the drone.
propwash.video.spectate.goggles_none: Put on goggles (head slot) to watch other pilots.
propwash.video.spectate.show_osd.tip: While spectating, shows the drone’s flight data (battery, speed, altitude, channel) in your OSD layout.
propwash.video.spectate.show_banner.tip: Shows channel, pilot and drone on a panel at the top of the picture.
propwash.video.spectate.tab_hint: Key %s: next active channel, after the last one spectating ends. Esc or right-click: back to yourself. You don’t control anything – you only see the picture.
propwash.video.spectate.result.not_found: This channel is no longer transmitting
propwash.video.spectate.result.rule_off: Spectating is turned off on this server
propwash.video.spectate.result.wrong_sys: Your goggles can’t receive this video system
propwash.video.spectate.result.piloting: Not possible while you are flying
propwash.video.spectate.result.other_dim: The drone is in another dimension
propwash.video.channel.footer: Channel and power: saved in the drone · spectating: all drones
propwash.video.channel.info_auto_digital: Automatic: at takeoff the server picks a free digital channel – CH1 to CH8 in order. The channel is shown in the OSD (VTX).

%s carries the Action Cam (Flashback), but Flashback (Fabric only) is not ready: this camera records nothing – neither a camera path nor a video.
propwash.video.record.tab.hint.flashback: %1$s starts and stops the camera path for Flashback – in FPV and in line of sight (rebind it in the “Keys” tab). On the radio: function “%2$s” in the “Modes” tab. The Action Cam (Flashback) records no video itself: resolution, frame rate, quality, stabilization and sound above only apply to the Action Cam (Light) and (Heavy).
propwash.video.record.tab.status.flashba: The camera path waits for Flashback (starting or paused)…
propwash.video.record.tab.hint.flashback: With the Action Cam (Flashback) on top, the same button records a camera path for Flashback instead of a video: open the replay in Flashback and pick the scene “Propwash · Flight …” to render, cut or change it.
propwash.video.flashback.toast.thinned: Thinned for Flashback's timeline: %s keyframes, up to %s cm / %s°.
propwash.video.flashback.toast.too_big: This scene is too large for Flashback's timeline. The game may crash when the replay is opened.
propwash.video.record.tab.flashback_simp: How much the camera path is simplified for Flashback. "Off" saves every tick. Further right, Propwash only keeps the points needed so that Flashback's camera stays within the shown distance of the real flight. The preview below shows the difference.
propwash.video.record.tab.flashback_limi: Flashback's timeline can only draw a limited number of keyframes at once, roughly 600 to 1,900 per flight depending on display scaling. Beyond that the game crashes when the replay is opened. With the limit on, Propwash thins long flights when saving so they fit; the path becomes a few centimetres less exact. The OSD element "Flashback timeline" shows how full the budget is. Without the limit every keyframe is kept, but long flights may not open.
propwash.video.record.tab.flashback_chec: Finds Flashback replays whose Propwash scenes are too large for Flashback's timeline and thins them on request. Propwash keeps a backup copy first.

propwash.input.modes.effect.vtx_power: Next transmit power (like a VTX table)
propwash.input.modes.desc.vtx_power: Steps the video transmitter to the next power level; after the highest it switches to Auto, then back to the lowest – like a VTX table in Betaflight, best on a button. Without an assignment the “Step VTX power” key (F10) does the same. More power means more range and better penetration, but it drains the battery and heats up the transmitter.
propwash.video.vtx.power.tip_digital: Transmit power of this drone. Auto (default) works like DJI and Walksnail and follows the link: low when close, up to the highest level with distance and obstacles. A fixed level stays as it is.
propwash.video.vtx.power.tip_analog: Transmit power of this drone. With Auto (default) the flight controller sets the power from the signal strength of your radio link: low when close, up to the highest level with distance and obstacles. Twice the power gives about 1.4× the range and 3 dB more against obstacles, but draws more current and heats up the transmitter.
propwash.video.vtx.low_power.tip: Like vtx_low_power_disarm in Betaflight: while the drone is disarmed it transmits at the lowest level. That spares the transmitter and battery on the ground and does not disturb other pilots. “Until first arm” transmits at full power again after a crash so you can find the drone.
propwash.video.vtx.info_none: Hold a drone in your hand or fly it to set its transmit power.
propwash.video.vtx.info_single: This video module always transmits at %s mW.
propwash.video.vtx.info_auto: Auto: %s mW close to the pilot, up to %s mW with distance and obstacles. Switch in flight with the “VTX power” switch or the %s key.
propwash.video.vtx.info_auto_analog: Auto: the flight controller follows the signal strength of your radio link (distance and obstacles) and keeps some reserve: %s mW close to the pilot, up to %s mW further out. Switch in flight with the “VTX power” switch or the %s key.
propwash.video.vtx.info_level: %s mW: range about %s blocks, video system %s W. Switch in flight with the “VTX power” switch or the %s key.
propwash.video.vtx.info_heat: Without airflow on the ground the transmitter overheats after about %s min and then turns itself down.
propwash.video.vtx.info_analog: Analog transmitters do not measure their own picture; with Auto the flight controller sets the power instead.
propwash.video.vtx.toast.single: This video module has only one level (%s mW)
